The benefit realization approach for Test should be framed around measurable supply chain outcomes that can be linked directly to business value through operational capabilities and supporting performance metrics. The available source material indicates that the relevant benefit areas include revenue, cost of goods sold, SG&A, and capital, with example value levers such as lost sale reduction, forecast accuracy improvement, planner efficiency, obsolete inventory reduction, inventory holding cost reduction, expedited freight reduction, inventory reduction, and network visibility. These measures provide the structure for how Test can define, track, and govern business value as part of its investment.

<IMAGE id="7621e142a076"/>

For Test, quantitative benefit tracking should therefore be established by connecting each targeted business outcome to the underlying capability that enables it and the metric that demonstrates improvement. The source material specifically points to benefit categories such as lost sale reduction, forecast accuracy, planner efficiency, obsolete inventory reduction, inventory holding cost, expedited freight, inventory reduction, and network visibility. These should be used as the basis for Test’s benefit measurement framework, with detailed baselines, targets, timing, and ownership marked as TBD where not available in Test source documents.

<IMAGE id="cdc0a0569a39"/>

The same source material also indicates that benefit realization in supply chain planning is typically mapped to shareholder value metrics through a capability-to-metric relationship. For Test, this means the business case should be expressed not only in terms of operational change, but in terms of how those changes influence revenue protection or growth, cost reduction, improved productivity, and working capital performance. Where Test-specific values, calculations, or expected ranges are not present in the source documents, they remain TBD. Accordingly, Test’s section on benefits should be treated as a structured framework for value realization, with client-specific quantified estimates to be completed from Test source documents or future validation.
